interpretation: This attributes the positive replacement account, not a verified proof that any selected immediate proposition is true or warranted. His accompanying necessity argument retains prior-premise knowledge and termination at immediates; this chapter does not itself supply the full acquisition account later pursued in II.19. No identification of the principle with a separately formalized nous predicate is installed. The horoi are rendered here as defining terms, not as mere lexical familiarity sufficient to warrant arbitrary propositions.
